fc.name: CubePilot Cube Orange+ Standard Set (ADS-B IN carrier board)

estimates.mass_g: Only the 33 g cube module is published; the 94.5 x 44.3 mm carrier board is estimated at 42 g.
estimates.rail_5v_range: CubePilot says peripherals see up to 5.5 V after filtering; 4.9 V lower bound assumes a 5.2 V brick minus the ideal diode drop.

fc.notes: mass_g is null: only the cube module mass (33 g, Airbot Systems vendor page) is published; no source gives the ADS-B carrier board mass (RMRC only lists a 0.55 lb shipping weight for the whole boxed set). Price is IR-LOCK list price (RMRC lists 450.99). Supply range: PX4 docs and IR-LOCK say 4.1 to 5.7 V / 2.5 A; CubePilot operating-conditions page says 4.1 to 5.5 V. The ArduPilot hwdef README still says STM32H743 in its feature list, but hwdef.dat declares STM32H757 and CubePilot confirms H757. Connector pin logic: ArduPilot documents 3.3 V signals; CubePilot interface spec writes '3.3 V - 5.0 V TTL', which is best read as 5 V tolerant inputs, not 5 V outputs. The standard set includes a CubePilot Power Brick Mini (Molex CLIK-Mate cable), which is plug-compatible with POWER1 and already matches the firmware default battery scaling.
findings: 0x10 unique on fc.I2C2 (the internal compass at 0x0C is on a separate internal bus)

bec12.name: Mateksys BEC12S-PRO (set to 12 V)
bec12.notes: Compatibility caveat for the checker: a 4S pack sags below 14 V late in the flight, at which point the 12 V output is no longer regulated and tracks input minus dropout. It stays well inside the Jetson 9 to 20 V window, so the Jetson keeps running. A second BEC12S-PRO left at its 5.2 V default is a clean way to power the RFD900x off the autopilot (RFD900x needs 5.0 to 5.5 V). Note the Jetson accepts 9 to 20 V directly, so a 4S pack (about 12 to 16.8 V) is inside its range even without a regulator; the regulator is there to isolate motor noise and transients.

gnss.name: CubePilot Here4 Multiband RTK GNSS

estimates.supply: Unpublished; 150 mA is the figure CubePilot staff give for earlier Here units, and the range is the Cube 5 V peripheral rail it is designed for.
estimates.terminated: Here4 ships as the end node of a CubePilot CAN bus; the Cube side is terminated on the carrier.

gnss.notes: Supply voltage and current are NOT published for Here4 (manual, IR-LOCK and RMRC pages all silent; a CubePilot forum thread only cites 150 mA for older Here units and 130 mA for the bare F9P during acquisition). It is powered from the 5 V CAN pin. The Here4 factory default of CAN_NODE is not documented; DNA is the normal behaviour. CubePilot SB_0000010 requires a Here4 bootloader update before flight on affected units.

estimates.typical_a: Unpublished; ESP8285 plus SX1281 at 100 mW telemetry.

rx.notes: Current draw is not published. UART logic level is not stated by RadioMaster; 3.3 V is inferred from the ESP8285 MCU (a 3.3 V part), flagged as logic_v_verified=false. The 5 V supply is a nominal 'DC 5V'; no tolerance band is published.

radio.name: RFDesign RFD900x-US telemetry modem
radio.notes: Can a Cube TELEM 5 V pin supply it? No. Datasheet peak is 1 A at 30 dBm; TELEM1 has a 1.5 A private limit, but CubePilot explicitly says never to power radios from carrier board connectors, TELEM2 sits in the shared 1 A group, and the whole peripheral budget is 2.5 A. Mass: datasheet says 14 g, RMRC lists 18 g. Supply: datasheet says +5 V min / +5.5 V max / +6 V absolute max, while RMRC says 3.5 V min; the datasheet is used. AIR_SPEED default is written '64/200' in the manual (footnoted), so 64 kbps is the usual SiK default but check the unit.

lidar.name: Benewake TFmini-S LiDAR (I2C mode)
lidar.notes: Chosen over the LightWare LW20/C because it is 5 g, cheap and supported in the stable build. LW20/C alternative for reference: RNGFND1_TYPE=7 (LightWareI2C), RNGFND1_ADDR=102 (0x66) per ArduPilot wiki. Supply is 5 V +/- 0.1 V per datasheet, so the Cube 5 V peripheral rail (up to 5.5 V after filtering per CubePilot) is nominally outside that tight band; in practice it is widely used this way, but the checker should flag it as a warning, not an error. Price not verified (retailer pages blocked or sold out). Ships in UART mode: send the "switch to I2C" command from the user manual once before wiring it to the I2C port.
findings: custom cable: JST-GH-4 to GH1.25-4P on sensor; Molex 51021-0400 (1.25 mm) on the 10 cm cable end
